correctness.rationale: The corner lemma exhausts opposite-corner allocations of the two remaining convex parts and yields explicit sharp alternatives. Vertical adjacent-corner pairs force min(Fv,Gv). Horizontal pairs are impossible for lambda>lambda0 by their own length, or imply Fh/Gh>=Fv via positive factors for lambda<=lambda0. Both formulas are attained by three explicit rectangles; exact identities replay in verify.py. No finite enumeration is claimed as an infinite proof.

evidence: Cañete–Fernández–Márquez, 2023, Theorem 3.3: diameter(C)/n < D_n(C) with orthotope-derived upper bound. Fekete et al., 2023, study three congruent disk covering as a subcase of disk weight, not an optimal small-diameter convex 3-partition.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A three-disk cover of radius r yields convex Voronoi-cell diameter at most 2r and so an upper bound. The converse fails without additional geometry: an equilateral triangle of side d has circumradius d/sqrt(3)>d/2. Therefore an exact least-radius three-disk covering theorem does not by itself force the required lower bound for convex partitions. This theorem proves that lower bound directly.

value.rationale: Complete real-parameter sharp minmax diameter classification for exactly 3 convex pieces of every rectangle, including a natural threshold at aspect ratio 3/2. Its global lower bound excludes all oblique, curved, and nonrectangular convex partitions, and it distinguishes the established lambda=1 endpoint from the new general profile. Natural benchmark for geometric division problems; no arbitrary extension or insignificant numerical refinement.
